title: Polynomial reduction of diagonal derived Hom over arbitrary rings
statement:
Let $R\to A$ be a flat finitely presented homomorphism of arbitrary commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Fix a surjection $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$, where $n\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Work in ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with derived tensor computed on K-flat resolutions and internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-object ringed site. Put $C=C_{P\to A}(P[0])[n]\in D(A)$, where $C_{P\to A}$ is derived coinduction with precomposition action $(a h)(a')=h(a'a)$ [def-trf-derived-coinduction]. Put $B=A\otimes_R A$, let $p_1:A\to B$ send $a$ to $a\otimes1$, and give $A$ its $B$-action via multiplication [def-trf-affine-diagonal-module-data]. For every $T\in D(A)$ there is an isomorphism in $D(A)$, natural in $T$,
$$\operatorname{Res}_{p_1}R\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,T\otimes_{A,p_1}^{\mathbf L}B)\ \cong\ R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,T).$$
Here restriction is along the first coprojection $A\to B$, not along multiplication $B\to A$. No pseudo-coherence, boundedness, or finite Tor hypothesis on $T$, and no Noetherian hypothesis on the rings, is imposed.

source.place: Agent mixed-ring polynomial-diagonal consequence of Tag 0A65, lemma-internal-hom (derived tensor--Hom adjunction), using perfect polynomial quotients and the ordered graph Koszul resolution. Derived-category isomorphism, not a cohomology-only comparison.

proof.text: Distinguish the two copies $A_1,A_2$ of $A$. Set $S=A_1\otimes_RP=A_1[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, $q:S\to B=A_1\otimes_RA_2$, $i:A_1\to S$, and $e=\mu q:S\to A$, where $\mu$ is multiplication. Write $a_j$ for the image of $x_j$ in $A$. Thus $e(x_j)=a_j$, $qi=p_1$ and $ei=1_A$. Put $D=C_{P\to A_2}(P[0])$, $E=C_q(S[0])$ and $V=S\otimes_{A_1}^{\mathbf L}T$. Then $C=D[n]$.

proof.text: The first conclusion of [lem-sfb-arbitrary-polynomial-dual-properties] gives a bounded finite projective $P$-resolution $F\to A_2[0]$. For any $P$-module $M$ the balanced isomorphism $M\otimes_PS\cong M\otimes_RA_1$, $m\otimes(a\otimes p)\mapsto pm\otimes a$, identifies tensoring with $S$ with tensoring over $R$ with the flat module $A_1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] this is exact. Hence $F\otimes_PS$ resolves $B[0]$; its terms are direct summands of finite free $S$-modules. In particular $B[0]$ is perfect over $S$, and $A_2,S$ are Tor independent over $P$: bounded finite projective complexes are K-flat by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat], so [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] computes their derived tensor by this resolution.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-perfect-coinduction-tor-independent-exchange] to $P\to A_2$, $P\to S$ and $M=P[0]$. The perfectness and Tor independence just established give $E\cong B\otimes_{A_2}^{\mathbf L}D$ in $D(B)$, where $A_2\to B$ is the second coprojection. This is an isomorphism with the precomposition $B$-action, not merely an isomorphism after forgetting scalars.

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat $A_2$-model $G$ of $D$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Its extension $B\otimes_{A_2}G$ is K-flat over $B$ by [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings]. Consequently [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] and Step 3 compute $A\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}E$ by $A\otimes_B(B\otimes_{A_2}G)\cong G$. The map is $a\otimes(b\otimes g)\mapsto a\mu(b)g$, with inverse $g\mapsto1\otimes(1\otimes g)$. Since $\mu p_2=1_A$, these are inverse balanced chain maps. The residual $S$-action is through $e$: $a_1\otimes p$ acts on $G$ as multiplication by $a_1\bar p$. Thus $\operatorname{Res}_q(A\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}E)\cong\operatorname{Res}_eD$ in $D(S)$.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-perfect-algebra-dual-evaluation], with $B$ perfect over $S$, $J_E(V)\cong B\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}V$ in $D(B)$, naturally in $V$. A flat-term K-flat $A_1$-model $H$ of $T$ exists by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]; $S\otimes_{A_1}H$ is K-flat over $S$ by [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings]. Using [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor], the inverse balanced chain maps $b\otimes(s\otimes h)\mapsto bq(s)\otimes h$ and $b\otimes h\mapsto b\otimes(1\otimes h)$ give $B\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}V\cong B\otimes_{A_1}^{\mathbf L}T$. They are $B$-linear and natural in $T$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-derived-bimodule-tensor-hom] to $q:S\to B$, $X=A$ with multiplication action, $E=C_q(S)$ and $V$. Steps 4 and 5 identify its two sides. Restrict its $D(S)$-isomorphism along $i:A_1\to S$, using $qi=p_1$, to obtain $$\operatorname{Res}_{p_1}R\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,T\otimes_{A_1}^{\mathbf L}B)\cong\operatorname{Res}_iR\operatorname{Hom}_S(\operatorname{Res}_eD,V).$$ No flatness of the multiplication map is used.

proof.text: The evaluation $e:S=A_1[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\to A$ is exactly the graph map with ordered equations $x_j-a_j$. Apply [lem-trf-polynomial-graph-coinduction] to obtain $C_e(V)\cong T[-n]$ in $D(A)$, naturally for every $T$, with its original $A$-action. Its hypotheses require neither Noetherianity nor boundedness or a Tor condition on $T$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-algebraic-shriek-derived-hom-adjunction] to $e:S\to A$, $X=D$ and $Y=V$. Its enriched isomorphism identifies $R\operatorname{Hom}_S(\operatorname{Res}_eD,V)$ with $\operatorname{Res}_eR\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,C_e(V))$. Restrict along $i$ and use $ei=1_A$ and Step 7. Step 6 therefore equals $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,T[-n])\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D[n],T)=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,T)$; the shift identification is the reindexing, with the cochain differential signs, of [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex]. Each constituent is a natural derived isomorphism, so their composite is natural in $T$. The construction includes $n=0$ and the zero ring, and never uses a finiteness hypothesis on $T$.

Step 5: dual-evaluation needs only B perfect over S, for arbitrary V; the cancellation uses qi=p_1. Step 6: the bimodule adjunction with X=A, restricted along i, gives the LHS. Step 7: graph-coinduction over base A_1. Step 8: shriek adjunction for e, then ei=1 and the shift reindexing.
